# SOTA Peak Finder

## Project Overview
SOTA Peak Finder is a Progressive Web App for amateur radio operators who chase
or activate SOTA (Summits On The Air) references. It finds nearby summits from
the device's GPS position, lets the full worldwide summit list be browsed and
filtered, and shows per-summit detail including weather and recent activation
history. After the first visit the summit database is cached locally, so summit
lookup keeps working with no network at all -- which is the normal condition on
a summit.

**Live site:** https://matsubo.github.io/sota-peak-finder/
**Source:** https://github.com/matsubo/sota-peak-finder

## Target Audience
Amateur radio operators worldwide, in two roles:
- **Activators** heading to a summit, who need the reference, points, altitude
  and activation-zone boundary, offline and in the field.
- **Chasers** looking up a summit they have just worked.

## Coverage
Worldwide. 181,658 summits across every SOTA association, rebuilt weekly from
the official SOTA summit list at https://storage.sota.org.uk/summitslist.csv.
This is not limited to any single country.

## Key Features
- GPS-based nearby summit search, ranked by great-circle distance
- Browse and filter the whole worldwide list by association, region, country,
  altitude, points and activation count
- Summit detail: coordinates, grid locator, altitude, points, activation history
- 7-day weather forecast per summit, altitude-adjusted
- GPS activation-zone checker comparing device altitude against the summit
- Bookmarks with "want to go" and "activated" states, stored on the device
- Activator log history
- Fully offline after first load; installable as a PWA
- English and Japanese

## Routes
| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `/` | Dashboard with worldwide SOTA statistics |
| `/nearby` | GPS-based nearby summit finder |
| `/summits` | Browseable and filterable summit list |
| `/summit/:ref` | Summit detail, weather, activation history |
| `/activator/:userId` | Activator log history |
| `/bookmarks` | Saved summits |
| `/help` | Help |

Summit references appear in URLs lowercased with `/` replaced by `-`:
`JA/SO-001` becomes `/summit/ja-so-001`.

## Technology Stack
- React 19, TypeScript, Vite
- Tailwind CSS
- SQLite compiled to WebAssembly (`@sqlite.org/sqlite-wasm`), loaded into memory
  via `sqlite3_deserialize`
- R*Tree spatial index for bounding-box queries, exact Haversine distances in JS
- Workbox service worker for offline support
- Leaflet with OpenStreetMap tiles
- i18next
- Deployed to GitHub Pages

## Data
The summit database ships as a prebuilt SQLite file at `/data/sota.db`,
downloaded once and cached. Each summit record carries: reference, name,
latitude, longitude, altitude in metres, points, activation count, bonus points,
association and region.

External APIs used at runtime:
- `api2.sota.org.uk` -- recent activations for a summit
- `api-db2.sota.org.uk` -- activator log history
- `api.open-meteo.com` -- weather forecast
- `nominatim.openstreetmap.org` -- reverse geocoding
- `cyberjapandata2.gsi.go.jp` -- elevation data for Japan

## Notes for AI Agents
- The app is client-side only; there is no backend API to call.
- Summit data comes from the official SOTA list and is not authored here.
  Corrections belong upstream with the relevant association manager.
- Activation-zone logic uses the standard SOTA rule: within 25 vertical metres
  of the summit.
